subject: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Team — quick summary: Polaris Labs executed a Dedicated commitment today for an 8-GPU reserved pool (A100s) starting Oct 1 for 12 months. Separately, AtlasGrove submitted an urgent add-on request that would allocate 10 GPUs from the same regional pool for Oct 1–Nov 30 (burst into reserved capacity). Both deals map to the same physical cluster in us-west-2 and our capacity plan shows a clear overlap on the node set we were about to pin for Polaris.

Polaris is high-touch (legal wants co-located SLAs) and revenue-retentive; AtlasGrove is a fast-growing strategic trial that is asking to burst immediately. We need a plan that preserves Polaris' reservation while offering AtlasGrove a feasible short-term option without violating our SLOs or existing product commitments.

Options I'm putting on the table for rapid decision:
- Carve Polaris onto explicit physical hosts (static reservation), move Atlas into the remaining pool with throttled preemption rules
- Offer AtlasGrove an alternate region burst (us-east-1) with cross-region latency caveats and a one-time credit
- Provide AtlasGrove a degraded quantized runtime (Q8) for the first 2 months at a reduced price to relieve pressure
- Accelerated billing / upfront payment from Polaris to secure node pinning and SLA addendum

Deadline: we need a recommended course of action and runbook by 2026-09-23 17:00 PT so Sales can communicate with both customers. Please reply with a concrete operational plan, list of steps, and any gating constraints (hardware moves, migration windows, expected latency impact).

Attachments: polaris_capacity_request.xlsx (requested config), preliminary cluster assignment snapshot attached.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Naomi —
Short answer: we can avoid an all-out preemption by leveraging two tactics in parallel.
1) Pin Polaris to host set H-3/H-4 (that cluster is healthy and can be isolated via reservation). That will reduce the remaining free capacity in us-west-2 but preserves their SLA expectations.
2) Offer AtlasGrove a burst to us-east-1 for the first 6 weeks. I attached a region map that shows spare capacity in us-east-1 that matches their GPU profile.

Downside: pinning eats some resiliency and may increase tail latency for on-demand workloads by ~15–20% if the rest of the pool gets noisy. We should add a temporary rate cap on the open pool for non-reserved tenants to keep latency bounded.

Attached: region_capacity_map.pdf

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive (Dedicated Sales)
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Team — operational constraints and a pragmatic runbook below.
1) Node pinning is doable but not instant. We need a maintenance window to mark hosts as reserved and migrate existing best-effort pods off them; estimate 6–10 hours for fence + verification per host. If Polaris signs the accelerated invoice and DS envelope, we can prioritize this change on Oct 1 morning.
2) Alternate-region burst: cross-region replication for model artifacts and KV cache will add ~80–120ms RTT on average and requires a short bootstrap copy (1–3 hours for standard models). We'll need AtlasGrove’s approval to accept higher latency.
3) Quantized/degraded runtime: we can cut AtlasGrove's token throughput by ~25–30% with Q8 paths and reduced batch sizes; latency per token marginally improves, but end-to-end throughput drops — appropriate for non-latency-sensitive batch inference.

Suggested mutual action plan (MVP):
- 09/22: Ops to reserve H-3/H-4 tentatively (no changes yet) and prepare migration playbook
- 09/23: Sales to confirm Polaris' willingness to sign accelerated billing and SLA addendum (DocuSign: ENVELOPE-54A3B8)
- 09/24: If Polaris signs, Ops executes pinning during Oct 1 maintenance window (6–10 hours)
- If Polaris does not sign, fallback to proportional throttling + prioritize AtlasGrove for queued burst with strict preemption rules

HubSpot references: HUB-9872 (Polaris), HUB-9944 (AtlasGrove). I've logged a high-severity runbook ticket in Jira for the change window.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity Planning & Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@polaris-labs.com>, Rajesh Srinivasan <rajesh@atlasgrove.ai>

Subject: FW: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Hi Emily / Rajesh — forwarding the internal runbook and proposed short-term options so you each have the same view. High-level proposals:
A) Polaris: pin dedicated hosts (preferred by Redwood to guarantee SLA) in exchange for accelerated billing / one-time reservation fee (we'll update contract Appendix A).
B) Atlas: short-term burst to an alternate region (us-east-1) OR temporary quantized runtime at reduced cost while we settle long-term capacity.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (simple checklist).

Can you confirm by 2026-09-23 which option you prefer and whether Polaris is open to the reservation fee / accelerated billing? If we don't have alignment, Ops will be forced to apply strict preemption rules which could impact AtlasGrove's throughput.

Thanks,
Naomi
From: Emily Chen <emily@polaris-labs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Naomi / team —
Polaris is willing to sign accelerated billing and pay a one-time reservation fee to secure pinned hosts, but we will require a written SLA credit clause for any outage >5 minutes affecting the reserved pool during the first 90 days. Please send redlined Appendix A with the proposed credit terms and we'll expedite legal review.

—Emily Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Polaris Labs

-----Original Message-----
From: Rajesh Srinivasan <rajesh@atlasgrove.ai>
Sent: 2026-09-22T16:42:00-07:00
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation conflict: Polaris Labs vs AtlasGrove — action required

Naomi —
AtlasGrove appreciates the alternative-region option but would prefer to avoid cross-region latency for customer-facing workloads. Our engineers can accept the quantized runtime tier for the first 8 weeks if Redwood can guarantee a throughput cap and a clear rollback path to full-precision once capacity is available. If Polaris proceeds with host pinning, please ensure the rollback timeline is published to us.

I'll have our legal coordinate with Ben on the exact credits if it comes to it.

Rajesh
CTO, AtlasGrove
